section.title: Downloading HarfBuzz
section.para: The HarfBuzz source code is hosted at github.com/harfbuzz/harfbuzz.

Tarball releases and Win32 binary bundles (which include the libharfbuzz DLL, hb-view.exe, hb-shape.exe, and all dependencies) of HarfBuzz can be downloaded from github.com/harfbuzz/harfbuzz/releases.

Release notes are posted with each new release to provide an overview of the changes. The project tracks bug reports and other issues on GitHub. Discussion and questions are welcome on GitHub as well.

The API included in the hb.h file will not change in a compatibility-breaking way in any release. However, other, peripheral headers are more likely to go through minor modifications. We will do our best to never change APIs in an incompatible way. We will never break the ABI.

section.title: Building on Linux
section.para: (1) To build HarfBuzz on Linux, you must first install the development packages for FreeType, Cairo, and GLib. The exact commands required for this step will vary depending on the Linux distribution you use.

For example, on an Ubuntu or Debian system, you would run: sudo apt install gcc g++ libfreetype6-dev libglib2.0-dev libcairo2-dev On Fedora, RHEL, CentOS, or other Red-Hat–based systems, you would run: sudo yum install gcc gcc-c++ freetype-devel glib2-devel cairo-devel
(2) The next step depends on whether you are building from the source in a downloaded release tarball or from the source directly from the git repository.
(2)(a) If you downloaded the HarfBuzz source code in a tarball, you can now extract the source.
From a shell in the top-level directory of the extracted source code, you can run meson setup build followed by meson compile -C build as with any other standard package.
This should leave you with a shared library in the src/ directory, and a few utility programs including hb-view and hb-shape under the util/ directory.

(2)(b) If you are building from the source in the HarfBuzz git repository, rather than installing from a downloaded tarball release, then you must install two more auxiliary tools before you can build for the first time: pkg-config.
On Ubuntu or Debian, run: sudo apt-get install meson pkg-config gtk-doc-tools On Fedora, RHEL, CentOS, run: sudo yum install meson pkgconfig gtk-doc
With pkg-config installed, you can now run meson setup build then meson compile -C build to build HarfBuzz.

section.title: Building on Windows
section.para: Install meson and run (from the console) meson setup build (by default bundled dependencies are not built, --wrap-mode=default overrides this), then meson compile -C build to build HarfBuzz.

section.title: Building on macOS
section.para: There are two ways to build HarfBuzz on Mac systems: MacPorts and Homebrew. The process is similar to the process used on a Linux system.
(1) You must first install the development packages for FreeType, Cairo, and GLib. If you are using MacPorts, you should run: sudo port install freetype glib2 cairo
If you are using Homebrew, you should run: brew install freetype glib cairo
(2) The next step depends on whether you are building from the source in a downloaded release tarball or from the source directly from the git repository.

(2)(a) If you are installing HarfBuzz from a downloaded tarball release, extract the tarball and open a Terminal in the extracted source-code directory. Run: meson setup build followed by: meson compile -C build to build HarfBuzz.
(2)(b) Alternatively, if you are building HarfBuzz from the source in the HarfBuzz git repository, then you must install several built-time dependencies before proceeding.
If you are using MacPorts, you should run: sudo port install meson pkgconfig gtk-doc to install the build dependencies.
If you are using Homebrew, you should run: brew install meson pkgconfig gtk-doc Finally, you can run: meson setup build
(3) You can now build HarfBuzz (on either a MacPorts or a Homebrew system) by running: meson setup build followed by: meson compile -C build
This should leave you with a shared library in the src/ directory, and a few utility programs including hb-view and hb-shape under the util/ directory.

section.title: Configuration options
section.para: The instructions in the "Building HarfBuzz" section will build the source code under its default configuration. If needed, the following additional configuration options are available.

listitem.para: Use GLib. (Default = auto)

This option enables or disables usage of the GLib library. The default setting is to check for the presence of GLib and, if it is found, build with GLib support. GLib is native to GNU/Linux systems but is available on other operating system as well.
Use GObject. (Default = auto)

This option enables or disables usage of the GObject library. The default setting is to check for the presence of GObject and, if it is found, build with GObject support. GObject is native to GNU/Linux systems but is available on other operating system as well.
Use Cairo. (Default = auto)
This option enables or disables usage of the Cairo graphics-rendering library. The default setting is to check for the presence of Cairo and, if it is found, build with Cairo support.
Note: Cairo is used only by the HarfBuzz command-line utilities, and not by the HarfBuzz library.
Use the ICU library. (Default = auto)

This option enables or disables usage of the International Components for Unicode (ICU) library, which provides access to Unicode Character Database (UCD) properties as well as normalization and conversion functions. The default setting is to check for the presence of ICU and, if it is found, build with ICU support.
Use the Graphite2 library. (Default = no)

This option enables or disables usage of the Graphite2 library, which provides support for the Graphite shaping model. A build with Graphite2 shapes fonts that have Graphite tables with it, not with the OpenType shaper.
Note: the older name of this option, -Dgraphite, is deprecated.
Use the FreeType library. (Default = auto)
This option enables or disables usage of the FreeType font-rendering library. The default setting is to check for the presence of FreeType and, if it is found, build with FreeType support.
Use the Uniscribe library (experimental). (Default = no)

This option enables or disables usage of the Uniscribe font-rendering library. Uniscribe is available on Windows systems. Uniscribe support is used only for testing purposes and does not need to be enabled for HarfBuzz to run on Windows systems.
Use the DirectWrite library (experimental). (Default = no)

This option enables or disables usage of the DirectWrite font-rendering library. DirectWrite is available on Windows systems. DirectWrite support is used only for testing purposes and does not need to be enabled for HarfBuzz to run on Windows systems.
Use the CoreText library. (Default = no)
This option enables or disables usage of the CoreText library. CoreText is available on macOS and iOS systems.
Use GTK-Doc. (Default = auto)
This option enables the building of the documentation.
Build the subsetting library. (Default = enabled)
This option enables or disables building libharfbuzz-subset, which subsets and instances fonts, and the hb-subset utility.
Build the rasterization library. (Default = enabled)
This option enables or disables building libharfbuzz-raster, which renders glyphs to pixels, and the hb-raster utility.
Build the vector drawing library. (Default = enabled)
This option enables or disables building libharfbuzz-vector, which writes glyphs as SVG or PDF, and the hb-vector utility.
Build the GPU rasterization library. (Default = enabled)
This option enables or disables building libharfbuzz-gpu, which encodes glyphs for rendering in a shader.
Build the command-line utilities. (Default = enabled)

This option enables or disables building hb-shape, hb-info, and the other utilities. They need GLib. hb-view is built only with Cairo, and the utility of each library above only when that library is built.
Use HarfRust. (Default = disabled)
This option enables or disables the HarfRust shaper backend. It needs a Rust toolchain.
Use Fontations. (Default = disabled)
This option enables or disables the Fontations font-functions backend. It needs a Rust toolchain.
Use kb_text_shape. (Default = disabled)
This option enables or disables the kb_text_shape shaper backend.
Build the WebAssembly shaper (experimental). (Default = disabled)

This option enables or disables the WebAssembly shaper, which runs the shaping code that a font carries in its Wasm table. It needs the WebAssembly Micro Runtime library. A build with it shapes fonts that have a Wasm table with it, not with the OpenType shaper.
Use libpng. (Default = auto)
This option enables or disables usage of libpng, which the rasterization library uses to read PNG glyph images and to write PNG output, and the utilities to write PNG output.
Use zlib. (Default = auto)
This option enables or disables usage of zlib, which is used to read compressed SVG glyph documents and to embed PNG glyph images in PDF output.
Use Chafa. (Default = auto)
This option enables or disables usage of the Chafa library, which the utilities use to show their output in a terminal.
Note: Chafa is used only by the HarfBuzz command-line utilities, and not by the HarfBuzz library.
Use GObject Introspection. (Default = auto)
This option enables or disables generating the introspection data (.gir and .typelib files) that language bindings are made from. It needs GObject support.
Build ICU support into the HarfBuzz library. (Default = false)
By default the ICU integration is a separate library, libharfbuzz-icu. This option builds it into libharfbuzz instead.
Build the experimental API. (Default = false)
This option enables the API that is marked experimental, which can change or be removed in any release.

section.para: The remaining options are for running the tests, benchmarks and fuzzers, and for packaging. The file meson_options.txt lists every option with its default, and meson configure build shows the value each has in a build directory.

section.title: Single-file build with harfbuzz-world.cc
section.para: For projects that want HarfBuzz embedded without any build-system glue, the source ships a single-file amalgamation at src/harfbuzz-world.cc that #includes every .cc in the library so the whole thing compiles as one translation unit. Pair it with the HB_TINY / HB_HAS_* compile-time switches (see Configuration options above) to pick which subsystems get pulled in.
A live in-browser playground built against this exact file lives at harfbuzz-world.cc; its source is a worked example of dropping HarfBuzz into a project.
